title: Attack threshold for a XOR-combination Even--Mansour schedule
summary: Determine whether the fixed four-round Even--Mansour schedule ending in K0 xor K1 can be attacked at total complexity 2^n.

formal_statement.body: Let $N=2^n$ and consider four-round iterated Even--Mansour with independent n-bit keys $K_0,K_1$, independent public round permutations, and fixed round-key sequence $[K_0,K_1,K_0,K_1,K_0\mathbin{\oplus}K_1]$. In the source classical known-plaintext model, does there exist a generic key-recovery attack with total time, data and memory complexity at most $N$ up to polynomial factors in $n$? If not, prove a security lower bound that excludes this $N=2^n$ threshold.

scope.domain: Generic classical cryptanalysis of a fixed four-round two-key iterated Even--Mansour key schedule
assumptions: The round-key sequence is exactly [K0,K1,K0,K1,K0 xor K1]
K0 and K1 are independent uniform n-bit keys
The public round permutations are independent random permutations
The source known-plaintext model counts time, data, memory and preprocessing
Multiplicative polynomial factors in n are ignored
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected classical result gives an attack of total complexity N=2^n or a lower bound excluding that threshold for the exact final-whitening schedule [K0,K1,K0,K1,K0 xor K1]. Quantum attacks on the strictly alternating schedule and attacks on other primitives do not cover this remainder.

provenance.note: The exact XOR-combination schedule is first stated as an unresolved example in the 2014-09-08 ePrint revision; it is not present in the first 2013-10-24 version.

progress.summary: A revised ePrint version fixes the schedule [K0,K1,K0,K1,K0 xor K1] and states that no attack of complexity 2^n was known, leaving an attack or a lower bound open.
